raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #27740 (closed by the stale bot; the bug is still on main).

With PD disaggregation, prefill can run pipeline parallel while decode runs PP=1. Plain MHA pools publish no layer IDs, so Mooncake (equal and heterogeneous TP), Mori and NIXL's heterogeneous-TP path place a prefill stage's K/V entries in decode's list by position (`get_mha_kv_ptrs_with_pp` or Mori's copy of it), treating `dst_num_total_layers % num_kv_layers != 0` as appended draft KV. An uneven split (7+8 of 15) takes that branch without any draft, so V lands in the wrong decode slots, and with a draft model the last stage also overwrites draft K. NIXL's equal-TP path rejects these transfers instead, because they need layer IDs.

## Modifications

`build_kv_layer_ids` now describes ordinary MHA registrations (`MHATokenToKVPool` itself, NHD layout, no KV quantization, two entries per layer) from the pool decode registers, so both peers use the layer-ID pairing hybrid pools already go through (`build_transfer_entry_pairs`), with the existing draft ID band and no new registration field. NIXL's heterogeneous-TP descriptors now pair the same way as Mooncake's `send_kvcache_slice`, and Mori's MHA pairing gets the `pp_size == 1` positional fallback the other paths apply.

With PP prefill, prefill and decode workers must be upgraded together: one-sided layer IDs are rejected (`Layer metadata must be provided by both PD peers or neither`), and on Mooncake and NIXL that stops a transfer worker or the prefill bootstrap thread rather than one request. `pd_disaggregation.mdx` describes this per backend. With PP=1 prefill, mixed versions keep positional pairing on all three backends. Quantized and special-layout MHA pools publish no layer IDs and keep the positional path, so they are not fixed here.

Related: #33497 by @zmtttt found the draft K overwrite on the last stage, and #33457 by @yhyang201 covers the hybrid-linear side.

## Accuracy Tests

On `604bcb8f3` (main `bce7b27aa`), `pytest -q test/registered/unit/disaggregation` gives 698 passed, 14 skipped, 358 subtests passed. Of the 10 new or renamed test methods, 7 fail on main and 3 guards (quantized pool, special layouts, unknown pool) pass on both; the Mori version-skew and NIXL heterogeneous-TP cases also fail with their source change reverted. isort, ruff, ruff-format and codespell pass on the changed files.

Rebased onto main `4eb606b2a` as `cbf865cd6`; the only change to the diff is one docstring sentence removed from `build_kv_layer_ids` (the upgrade guidance stays in `pd_disaggregation.mdx`), and main has not touched `srt/disaggregation` or `memory_pool.py` since `bce7b27aa`. On `cbf865cd6`, `pytest -q test/registered/unit/disaggregation` gives 698 passed, 14 skipped.

Real Mooncake TCP copies between two processes on one RTX PRO 6000, through the production equal-TP planner with IDs from the real pool builder (fixture managers, logical stage partitions, main `4fc86f73c`; these files are unchanged since): main corrupts every uneven case (11,520 or 21,504 target elements, plus 768 or 1,536 draft elements with a draft) and only the 8+8 control matches; the patch matches all six cases. Mori and NIXL are covered by the CPU tests only, and full PP serving across GPUs was not run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No end-to-end claim. Ordinary MHA transfers now pay the ID pairing: 7 to 34 us per call for 28 to 128 layers in a CPU microbenchmark (median of 7 x 10,000 calls), against under 1 us for `get_mha_kv_ptrs_with_pp`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

> [!WARNING]
> You have reached your daily quota limit. Please wait up to 24 hours and I will start processing your requests again!

Heads up — opened #33497 for the same underlying `get_mha_kv_ptrs_with_pp` case-3 arithmetic error, arrived at independently from a Qwen3.5-397B W4A8 + MTP/NEXTN + `PP=4` 3/4/4/4 production repro. Cross-linking so the maintainers can pick the shape they prefer.

Two differences worth flagging vs this PR:

* This PR passes `prefill_num_total_layers` in the sender direction; #33497 passes `num_target_kv_layers` in the **receiver** direction (single trailing ZMQ frame at position 18, `-1` sentinel for wire-back-compat). The invariant "target-then-draft layout" is owned by the receiver, so the receiver-side snapshot keeps the change local to `common/conn.py`.
* With MTP the overrun also **clobbers the first draft-K pointer** on the last PP rank, on top of the target-V drift; this shows up as spec_accept_rate collapsing (not just garbled text). #33497's unit test guards against that specifically.

Happy to close #33497 and fold its test / repro into this PR if you'd rather keep the sender-side approach — either resolution works for us as long as one lands.

Thanks for the cross-link and concrete repro. I rebased #28229 onto current main and folded the three complementary pieces into one patch: the decode-owned target-layer count and draft-K guard from #33497, the hybrid global-to-dense PP offset and exact layer-ID pairing from #33457, and #28229 removal of the ambiguous modulo heuristic for plain uneven PP.

The combined head is `819af38ce`. Registered disaggregation coverage passes with `102 passed, 22 subtests`, including the 15+1 MTP layout across 3/4/4/4 stages, one-sided MTP metadata, wire compatibility, and DCP/generic/slice forwarding. Black, isort, Ruff, compileall, diff-check, and fresh independent verification also pass.

This should now cover both the original no-draft uneven-PP failure and the hybrid/MTP draft-K corruption path in one PR. #33497 and #33457 are credited in the commit and updated description.

We independently hit the hybrid-model (GDN + full-attention) prefill-PP KV indexing bug on v0.5.18 + Mooncake, and can confirm the layer-id pairing approach in this PR fixes it on real hardware.

**Setup**: Qwen3.6-27B (48 layers, `full_attention_interval=4`), PD disaggregation over Mooncake (rdma), equal TP — P: tp1 **pp2**, D: tp1 pp1, on A100.

**Symptom on stock v0.5.18**: stage 0 transfers fine, stage 1 fails with `Prefill transfer kvcache error, layers_current_pp_stage is out of range: layers_current_pp_stage=6, len(dst_k_ptrs)=0`. This is the even-split sibling of the uneven-split mis-detection in #27740: `get_mha_kv_ptrs_with_pp` slices the decode-side dense KV list with `prefill_start_layer`, which counts the GDN layers too (stage 1: `start_layer=24` against a 12-entry K list → empty slice).

**What we verified**: we applied the same gate-promotion semantics as this PR's `_send_kvcache_generic` change (route the MHA layout to `build_transfer_entry_pairs` when both peers advertise `kv_layer_ids` — v0.5.18 already exchanges them in the registration frames) onto v0.5.18 and re-ran the failing scenario:
- The stage-1 transfer failure is gone; requests complete through both pipeline stages (3/3).
- Greedy outputs (temperature 0, 5 prompts × 64 tokens) match a pp1 baseline exactly on 4/5 prompts; the remaining one differs by a single near-tie token flip ("globally renowned" vs "renowned worldwide") that re-converges to an identical suffix — consistent with pp microbatching numerics, not mis-paired KV.

Hope this helps move the review along — happy to share more details from our runs if useful.

@zmtttt a correction to my August comment: after the rework, this PR pairs ordinary MHA KV by layer ID across uneven prefill PP stages, which also keeps decode's draft entries separate for unquantized NHD pools. It no longer includes #33497's receiver-side target-layer count or #33457's hybrid global-to-dense offset, and quantized or special-layout MHA pools keep the positional path, so neither PR is replaced by this one.

@@ -20,6 +20,23 @@ For the design details, please refer to [link](https://docs.google.com/document/
 
 Currently, we support Mooncake and NIXL as the transfer engine.
 
+## Pipeline-parallel worker upgrades
+
+Ordinary MHA KV pools (NHD layout, no KV quantization) publish KV layer IDs, and
+transfers pair their entries by layer ID, as they already do for hybrid pools.
+With pipeline-parallel prefill, upgrade prefill and decode workers together: a
+pair where only one side publishes layer IDs is rejected with `Layer metadata
+must be provided by both PD peers or neither`. Mooncake and NIXL reject it even
+when both peers register the same number of entries, because matching counts do
+not establish matching layer spans; Mori rejects it when the counts differ. The
+rejection is not limited to one request on Mooncake and NIXL. On Mooncake it ends
+the transfer worker thread that hit it, which logs that the prefill instance is
+dead. On NIXL it ends the prefill rank's bootstrap thread, and requests to that
+rank then time out in `KVPoll.Bootstrapping`. Mori fails only the affected
+request. With single-stage (PP=1) prefill, mixed versions keep positional
+pairing on all three backends. Drain in-flight requests before restarting both
+roles.
+
 ## Decode allocation policy
 
 By default, decode reserves each request's destination KV slots before prefill

+    """

+    @staticmethod
+    def _pool(start, layers, quant_method=None):
+        return MHATokenToKVPool(
+            size=3,
+            page_size=1,

+            head_num=2,
+            head_dim=4,
+            layer_num=layers,
+            device="cpu",

+            enable_alt_stream=False,

+            quant_method=quant_method,

+    @staticmethod
+    def _ids(target, draft=None):
+        return build_kv_layer_ids(
+            token_to_kv_pool=target,
+            draft_token_to_kv_pool=draft,
+            num_draft_entries=0 if draft is None else 2 * draft.layer_num,

+    def test_uneven_stages_copy_target_and_separate_draft_entries(self):

+        ):
+            with self.subTest(
+                source_draft=source_draft, destination_draft=destination_draft
+            ):
+                target = self._pool(0, 15)
+                draft = self._pool(0, 1) if destination_draft else None
+                dst = target.k_buffer + target.v_buffer
+                if draft is not None:
+                    dst += draft.k_buffer + draft.v_buffer
+                for tensor in dst:
+                    tensor.fill_(-1)
+                dst_ids = self._ids(target, draft)
+                for start, layers in ((0, 7), (7, 8)):
+                    source = self._pool(start, layers)
+                    for bias, buffers in (
+                        (10, source.k_buffer),
+                        (100, source.v_buffer),
+                    ):
+                        for index, tensor in enumerate(buffers):
+                            tensor.fill_(bias + start + index)
+                    # PD-prefill draft buffers belong to the final stage.
+                    src_draft = (
+                        self._pool(0, 1) if source_draft and start == 7 else None
+                    )
+                    src = source.k_buffer + source.v_buffer
+                    if src_draft is not None:
+                        src_draft.k_buffer[0].fill_(201)
+                        src_draft.v_buffer[0].fill_(202)

Heads up — opened #33497 for the same underlying `get_mha_kv_ptrs_with_pp` case-3 arithmetic error, arrived at independently from a Qwen3.5-397B W4A8 + MTP/NEXTN + `PP=4` 3/4/4/4 production repro. Cross-linking so the maintainers can pick the shape they prefer.

Two differences worth flagging vs this PR:

* This PR passes `prefill_num_total_layers` in the sender direction; #33497 passes `num_target_kv_layers` in the **receiver** direction (single trailing ZMQ frame at position 18, `-1` sentinel for wire-back-compat). The invariant "target-then-draft layout" is owned by the receiver, so the receiver-side snapshot keeps the change local to `common/conn.py`.
* With MTP the overrun also **clobbers the first draft-K pointer** on the last PP rank, on top of the target-V drift; this shows up as spec_accept_rate collapsing (not just garbled text). #33497's unit test guards against that specifically.

Happy to close #33497 and fold its test / repro into this PR if you'd rather keep the sender-side approach — either resolution works for us as long as one lands.

Thanks for the cross-link and concrete repro. I rebased #28229 onto current main and folded the three complementary pieces into one patch: the decode-owned target-layer count and draft-K guard from #33497, the hybrid global-to-dense PP offset and exact layer-ID pairing from #33457, and #28229 removal of the ambiguous modulo heuristic for plain uneven PP.

The combined head is `819af38ce`. Registered disaggregation coverage passes with `102 passed, 22 subtests`, including the 15+1 MTP layout across 3/4/4/4 stages, one-sided MTP metadata, wire compatibility, and DCP/generic/slice forwarding. Black, isort, Ruff, compileall, diff-check, and fresh independent verification also pass.

This should now cover both the original no-draft uneven-PP failure and the hybrid/MTP draft-K corruption path in one PR. #33497 and #33457 are credited in the commit and updated description.

We independently hit the hybrid-model (GDN + full-attention) prefill-PP KV indexing bug on v0.5.18 + Mooncake, and can confirm the layer-id pairing approach in this PR fixes it on real hardware.

**Setup**: Qwen3.6-27B (48 layers, `full_attention_interval=4`), PD disaggregation over Mooncake (rdma), equal TP — P: tp1 **pp2**, D: tp1 pp1, on A100.

**Symptom on stock v0.5.18**: stage 0 transfers fine, stage 1 fails with `Prefill transfer kvcache error, layers_current_pp_stage is out of range: layers_current_pp_stage=6, len(dst_k_ptrs)=0`. This is the even-split sibling of the uneven-split mis-detection in #27740: `get_mha_kv_ptrs_with_pp` slices the decode-side dense KV list with `prefill_start_layer`, which counts the GDN layers too (stage 1: `start_layer=24` against a 12-entry K list → empty slice).

**What we verified**: we applied the same gate-promotion semantics as this PR's `_send_kvcache_generic` change (route the MHA layout to `build_transfer_entry_pairs` when both peers advertise `kv_layer_ids` — v0.5.18 already exchanges them in the registration frames) onto v0.5.18 and re-ran the failing scenario:
- The stage-1 transfer failure is gone; requests complete through both pipeline stages (3/3).
- Greedy outputs (temperature 0, 5 prompts × 64 tokens) match a pp1 baseline exactly on 4/5 prompts; the remaining one differs by a single near-tie token flip ("globally renowned" vs "renowned worldwide") that re-converges to an identical suffix — consistent with pp microbatching numerics, not mis-paired KV.

Hope this helps move the review along — happy to share more details from our runs if useful.

@zmtttt a correction to my August comment: after the rework, this PR pairs ordinary MHA KV by layer ID across uneven prefill PP stages, which also keeps decode's draft entries separate for unquantized NHD pools. It no longer includes #33497's receiver-side target-layer count or #33457's hybrid global-to-dense offset, and quantized or special-layout MHA pools keep the positional path, so neither PR is replaced by this one.
